chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya who said:

I was with Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) when Al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi entered and said to him, 'May I be your ransom! I intend to go to A'wadh.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Wherever you find health and security, stick to it.' That did not satisfy him, so he set out intending to go to A'wadh, but the road was cut off (by bandits) and everything he had with him from wealth was taken.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, the eighth Imam
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ الصَّيْرَفِيُّ: Al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi, a companion known as the money-changer
key_terms.قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّرِيق: The road was cut off (idiom for being attacked by bandits)

ai.seo_question: What happened when Al-Husayn ibn Khalid ignored Imam al-Rida's advice to stay in A'wadh?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the practical wisdom of Imam al-Rida (AS) through his advice to Al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi to prioritize safety over travel, a lesson validated when the latter was robbed despite his insistence. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hikmah* (wisdom) and the importance of heeding the Imam's guidance in worldly affairs to avoid loss. The incident serves as a tangible example of the Imam's foresight and the consequences of disregarding his prudent counsel.
